title: Ordinary inner horn cell maps are inner anodyne in discrete space-valued presheaves
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and inner horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the space-valued presheaves of [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. Write $P(\Delta)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, where $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of small spaces, and for a small simplicial set $K$ write $dK\in P(\Delta)$ for the presheaf whose value at $[k]$ is the discrete space $K_k$; this is functorial in $K$. Let $\mathcal A_\Delta$ be the smallest class of arrows of $P(\Delta)$ containing $d(\Lambda^a_b\hookrightarrow\Delta^a)$ for all $a\geq2$, $0<b<a$, and closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts, all formed in the infinity category $P(\Delta)$. Let $u:K\to L$ be a map of small simplicial sets that is a retract, in the arrow category of simplicial sets, of a small transfinite composite, continuous at every nonzero limit stage, of pushouts of small coproducts (possibly empty) of inner horn inclusions $\Lambda^a_b\hookrightarrow\Delta^a$, $a\geq2$, $0<b<a$, where all these colimits are formed degreewise in sets. Then $du\in\mathcal A_\Delta$.

source.place: Haugseng, Definition 6.1 (weakly saturated classes in P(Delta)) and proof of Corollary 7.4, which applies Proposition 6.9 to the known inner-horn filtration of the ordinary simplicial-set pushout-product; the comparison between degreewise cell complexes and colimits in P(Delta) is used there without comment. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived (WANTED in the item report). No Stacks tag covers space-valued presheaves.

proof.text: For a set $S$, write $D(S)$ for the constant simplicial set on $S$, a Kan complex representing its discrete space. Work in the Kan model structure: by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] its cofibrations are monomorphisms, so all objects are cofibrant, and its fibrant objects are Kan complexes. By [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] it is combinatorial and simplicial. Thus [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies its infinity localization with $\mathcal S$ and computes maps from a cofibrant object to a Kan complex by the usual simplicial mapping set. In particular, for every Kan complex $T$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(D(S),T)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Fun}(D(S),T)=\prod_{s\in S}T$: in each simplicial degree a map is precisely one simplex of $T$ for each $s$. This formula is natural in set maps and in $T$, including $S=\varnothing$.

source.place: Example A.3.2.18 and Theorem 4.2.4.1; model and mapping comparisons are supplied by the cited nodes.

proof.text:
For one successor attachment write $X'=X\amalg_A B$, where $A\hookrightarrow B$ is a small coproduct of inner horn inclusions. Fix degree $n$ and put $C=B_n\setminus A_n$, so $B_n=A_n\amalg C$ and $X'_n=X_n\amalg C$, even when $A_n\to X_n$ is not injective. By Step 1, restriction of maps into a Kan complex $T$ along $A_n\hookrightarrow B_n$ is the projection $T^{A_n}\times T^C\to T^{A_n}$. This is a Kan fibration: for a horn lifting problem keep the prescribed first coordinates and fill the horn in each $C$-coordinate using the Kan property of $T$. The homotopy-pullback clause of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore computes
$$T^{X_n}\times^h_{T^{A_n}}T^{B_n}\simeq T^{X_n}\times T^C=T^{X'_n}.$$
The map from the last term to the pullback is exactly restriction along the set-pushout cocone. The colimit mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] proves that this specified cocone is a pushout in spaces. Its objectwise-colimit clause then shows $dX'\simeq dX\amalg_{dA}dB$ in $P(\Delta)$. These are the canonical cocone comparisons, so they are compatible with the simplicial operators, without requiring the complements $C$ themselves to be simplicial subsets.

source.place: Definition 6.1 and the unlabelled cell argument in the proof of Corollary 7.4; agent expansion of the discrete-space comparison.

proof.text:
Let $\lambda$ be a small nonzero limit ordinal in the given continuous cell construction. In degree $n$, take the strict $\lambda$-diagram $E_\alpha=D((X_\alpha)_n)$ of simplicial sets. Its degreewise colimit is $D((X_\lambda)_n)$, because continuity gives the corresponding set colimit. The category $\lambda$ is nonempty and filtered: a finite collection of ordinals below $\lambda$ has an upper bound below $\lambda$. Apply [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] in the combinatorial Kan model structure of Step 1 and choose a projectively cofibrant replacement $QE\to E$. Its ordinary colimit, with its specified cocone, becomes the coherent colimit of $E$ after localization. The replacement is objectwise a weak homotopy equivalence, so [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences] makes
$$\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\lambda}QE_\alpha\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\lambda}E_\alpha=D((X_\lambda)_n)$$
a weak homotopy equivalence. Under the comparison with spaces from Step 1 it is an equivalence and identifies the canonical set-colimit cocone with the coherent colimit. By the objectwise clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], the canonical cocone $dX_\alpha\to dX_\lambda$ is colimiting in $P(\Delta)$. Thus the limit stage is justified by the cited replacement and filtered-colimit theorems, rather than by assuming that $d$ preserves arbitrary colimits.

source.place: Definition 6.1 and the unlabelled cell argument in the proof of Corollary 7.4; agent expansion of the discrete-space comparison.

proof.text:
The class $\mathcal A_\Delta$ also contains small coproducts of its generating horn maps. To check this using only its stated closure operations, well-order a small family $h_j:A_j\hookrightarrow B_j$ of inner horns by an ordinal $\mu$. Set
$$Y_\beta=\left(\coprod_{j<\beta}B_j\right)\amalg\left(\coprod_{\beta\leq j<\mu}A_j\right)\quad(\beta\leq\mu).$$
Each $Y_\beta\to Y_{\beta+1}$ is the pushout of $h_\beta$ along its summand inclusion; Step 2 carries this square to a pushout in $P(\Delta)$. At a nonzero limit stage the degreewise union is $Y_\beta$, so Step 3 makes this a continuous chain after $d$. Small discrete coproducts become coproducts of spaces by the product formula for mapping spaces in Step 1, and hence coproducts of presheaves by the objectwise clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. The endpoints are therefore the coproducts of $dA_j$ and $dB_j$. Closure under transfinite composition puts their map in $\mathcal A_\Delta$. For the empty family it is the identity of the initial object, the empty transfinite composite. Consequently Step 2 sends every original successor attachment to a pushout of a map in $\mathcal A_\Delta$.

source.place: Definition 6.1 and the unlabelled cell argument in the proof of Corollary 7.4; agent expansion of the discrete-space comparison.

proof.text: Choose the arrow-category retract presentation assumed for $u$, and write $v:X_0\to X_\theta$ for the unretracted continuous cell composite. The preceding step puts every successor map $dX_\alpha\to dX_{\alpha+1}$ in $\mathcal A_\Delta$, and Step 3 verifies continuity at every nonzero limit stage. Closure under small transfinite compositions gives $dv\in\mathcal A_\Delta$ (including a zero-length composite). Applying the functor $d$ to the entire retract diagram preserves its identity composites, so $du$ is an arrow-category retract of $dv$. The defining retract closure gives $du\in\mathcal A_\Delta$.

So the homotopy-pullback clause on a cospan of Kan complexes, the colimit mapping-space criterion and the objectwise clause of lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits give the pushout in P(Delta). Step 3: lambda is filtered; lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison applies with no cofibrancy assumption on D, and lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences has no injectivity hypothesis.
